stories.title: Clark Solo Leads BMW Championship After Round 2 — Woodland Storms Off Bubble
stories.angle: Clark dominance + Woodland bubble story + Scheffler comeback charge

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
Wyndham Clark is running away with the BMW Championship.

Back-to-back 64s at Bellerive. -12 through 36 holes, solo lead.

Woodland -11. Spaun -10. Gotterup -9.

Scheffler moved to -5 with a back-nine 30.

R3 is Saturday. 🏌️

#BMWChampionship #FedExCup #PGATour

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Clark 64-64 = -12 at Bellerive.

Woodland one back at -11 — and he's moved off the FedExCup bubble.

He entered the week at 31st. He's now inside top 30.

This is what the playoffs are for. #FedExCup #PGATour

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:00 AM ET

Wyndham Clark has turned the BMW Championship at Bellerive Country Club into a showcase.

Clark shot a second consecutive 64 on Friday to reach -12 through 36 holes, taking the solo lead in this FedExCup Playoffs event. Back-to-back rounds of 64 on a par-70 layout represent elite, sustained ball-striking that has separated him from one of the best fields in golf.

Gary Woodland (-11) is one shot back — and carrying a compelling side story. He entered the week at 31st in the FedExCup standings, one spot outside the top 30 that earn a Tour Championship spot at East Lake. His 64-65 start has moved him inside the bubble.

J.J. Spaun (-10) and Chris Gotterup (-9) round out the top four. Scottie Scheffler, who opened at +2, fired a back-nine 30 in Round 2 to move to -5 — still seven back of Clark, but moving in the right direction.

Round 3 is Saturday at Bellerive. Top 30 after BMW advance to East Lake (Aug 27-30). ⛳

article.headline: Clark Shoots Back-to-Back 64s to Lead BMW Championship; Woodland Storms Off FedExCup Bubble

stories.title: Yamashita Sets 36-Hole Tournament Record at CPKC Women's Open — Leads by 5
stories.angle: Yamashita dominance, historic pace, Korda lurking

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
Miyu Yamashita just rewrote the CPKC Women's Open record book.

62-64 = 126. -14 through 36 holes.

New 36-hole tournament scoring record at Royal Mayfair.

Leads by 5 over World No. 1 Nelly Korda.

R3 Saturday. 🇯🇵⛳

#CPKCWomensOpen #LPGA

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
Yamashita -14.
Korda -9.

Five shots. Two rounds left.

The LPGA's biggest matchup of the summer starts Saturday in Edmonton.

#CPKCWomensOpen #NellyKorda #LPGA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:30 AM ET

Miyu Yamashita is playing historic golf in Edmonton.

The Japanese star shot a second-round 64 at Royal Mayfair GC on Friday to reach -14 (62-64=126) through 36 holes at the CPKC Women's Open. That 126 is the 36-hole scoring record at this tournament, broken on a par-70 Stanley Thompson-designed layout that demands precision and course management.

More importantly, Yamashita leads by five shots. World No. 1 Nelly Korda is in second place at -9.

A five-shot lead over the best player in the world is a remarkable position entering the weekend of a $2.75M LPGA event. But 36 holes remain, and Korda has the ability to make up ground quickly when the conditions are right.

Defending champion Brooke Henderson is also in the field. Round 3 is Saturday at Royal Mayfair. Golf Channel has coverage. ⛳🇯🇵

article.headline: Yamashita Sets 36-Hole Scoring Record at CPKC Women's Open, Leads by Five Over Korda

stories.title: FedExCup Bubble — Woodland Off, Fowler Clinging to 30th
stories.angle: Bubble drama, Woodland hero run, Fowler fighting to hold his spot

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
FedExCup bubble update after BMW R2:

Woodland entered week at 31st — outside looking in.

After 64-65 at Bellerive, he's inside the top 30.

Fowler entered at exactly 30th. Now under pressure.

R3 Saturday reshapes everything. #FedExCup #PGATour

facebook.long_form:
Window: 1:00 PM ET

The FedExCup bubble is shifting at Bellerive.

Gary Woodland entered the BMW Championship at 31st in the FedExCup standings — one spot outside the top 30 that advance to the Tour Championship at East Lake. His Round 1 64 was a statement. His Round 2 65 moved him inside the bubble.

Rickie Fowler entered the week at exactly 30th — the last qualifying spot for East Lake. As Woodland climbs, Fowler's position comes under pressure. FedExCup standings recalculate after each round, so Saturday's play at Bellerive reshapes the picture again.

Steve Cauley entered at 29th. Every position in the 25th-through-35th range has real consequences this week.

For Woodland, this is more than a golf tournament. It is a late-career run at a season lifeline. Right now, he is on the right side of the line.

Tour Championship at East Lake runs August 27-30. The bubble is very much alive. #FedExCup #PGATour

article.headline: FedExCup Bubble Shifts at Bellerive: Woodland Moves Inside Top 30, Fowler Under Pressure

stories.title: Scheffler Needs Historic Weekend — World No. 1 Seven Back at BMW
stories.angle: Scheffler needing a miracle run, back-nine surge as momentum signal

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Scottie Scheffler was +2 after Round 1.

Back nine of Round 2? He shot 30.

Now sits at -5. Seven back of Clark. World No. 1 isn't done yet.

#Scheffler #BMWChampionship #PGATour

facebook.long_form:
Window: 3:30 PM ET

Scottie Scheffler arrived at Bellerive Country Club as the World No. 1 and FedExCup top seed. His first round — a +2 — left him well outside the top 10 and eight shots off the lead.

On Friday, something changed. Scheffler's back nine in Round 2 was 30 strokes. He finished at -5 through 36 holes, moving from T44 to within striking distance of the weekend conversation.

He is still seven shots back of Wyndham Clark. Clark has been exceptional, and a seven-shot deficit over two rounds is a significant gap against a player in this form.

But the World No. 1 does not play for East Lake positioning alone. He plays to win. The back-nine 30 says his game has arrived at Bellerive — the question Saturday is whether he can carry that into the front nine and start a real title charge.

R3 is Saturday. Watch Scheffler's opening holes. #Scheffler #BMWChampionship #PGATour

article.headline: Scheffler Trails by Seven After BMW R2, But Back-Nine 30 Signals His Game Is Arriving

stories.title: CPKC Women's Open R3 Preview — Can Anyone Chase Down Yamashita?
stories.angle: Preview/anticipation, Yamashita vs. Korda, defending champ Henderson storyline

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
CPKC Women's Open R3 preview:

Yamashita -14 (5-shot lead)
Korda -9 (World No. 1)
Henderson in field (defending champ)

History on the line Saturday in Edmonton.

Who closes the gap? ⛳

#CPKCWomensOpen #LPGA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 6:00 PM ET

Saturday at Royal Mayfair Golf Club in Edmonton has one central question: can anyone chase down Miyu Yamashita?

Yamashita enters Round 3 of the CPKC Women's Open at -14 — five shots clear of World No. 1 Nelly Korda, who sits at -9. Two rounds remain at this $2.75M LPGA event.

A five-shot lead is significant but not insurmountable. Korda's ability to shoot low quickly is well-documented. A 63 on Saturday would pull her within two. A 62 would make it a one-shot game heading into Sunday.

Defending champion Brooke Henderson — who won the 2025 edition by one shot over Minjee Lee — is in the field. Lydia Ko, who famously won her first professional title at Royal Mayfair in 2013 as the youngest LPGA winner in history at age 15, is chasing a fourth CPKC title.

Golf Channel has coverage Saturday. This tournament has delivered historic scoring so far. Saturday has every reason to continue that trend. ⛳

article.headline: CPKC Women's Open R3 Preview: Yamashita's Five-Shot Lead vs. Korda's Chasing Power
